messages:
sam r: Quick heads-up — did a walkthrough of the new Alerting SLO canvas. The little status dots in the compact header are confusing when you have mixed metric types (p50 latency + error rate). Users asked what the dots map to.

elena p: Yep. They see 3 colors but no context. My suggestion: convert the tiny dots into labelled micro-pills: e.g. [OK · <80%] [Warn · 80-90%] [Breach · >=90%]. Keeps semantics + numbers in one glance.

noah g: Micro-pills are good. For people who need color-blind support, I prototyped thin SVG patterns (diagonal lines / dots) inside the pill rather than relying on background hatches — scales better at small sizes.

aria chen: That SVG pattern sounds promising. Can you drop the snippet? We need something that remains visible at 10px height.

noah g: Sure. Example SVG we tested: <svg width=12 height=12 role="img"><rect width=12 height=12 fill="#ef4444"></rect><path d="M0,3 L12,3 M0,6 L12,6" stroke="rgba(255,255,255,0.2)" stroke-width=1/></svg>. Keeps contrast and texture.

elena p: Also propose collapsing the legend into a single icon on narrow screens that opens a tray with full labels. The tray should announce "Legend: status definitions" to screen readers.

sam r: On collapse behavior: prefer a small affordance that shows primary state + a count like "OK +2" instead of a generic icon. Helps users know theres more. Make that trigger focusable and toggleable with Enter/Space.

aria chen: Accessibility bits: use aria-labelledby for each pill linking to a visually-hidden long description that reads the numeric bounds and the metric unit. E.g., aria-labelledby="pill-ok-desc" where the hidden node contains "OK: error rate less than 80 percent".

noah g: For keyboard users: when tray opens set focus to the first legend row and trap focus. When tray closes return focus to the trigger. Also include Esc to close.

elena p: Another nit: the preview button text currently reads "Preview notifications" but the canvas also shows routing, channel order, and the rendered message body. Could be "Preview routing & message" or shorten to "Preview routing" and add a tooltip explaining it includes message rendering.

sam r: We tried short labels in usability tests — they often truncate on narrow panes. To avoid truncation, put the full verboseness in the tooltip and use an icon + short label on the button e.g., [bell icon] Preview. Tooltip: "Preview routing and message rendering (channels, order, content)".

aria chen: Good call. Also ensure the preview's DOM order matches the channel stack order visually (first channel listed = first in DOM). We had a mismatch that made VoiceOver read in the opposite order.

noah g: For visual density: set a compact mode that reduces pill padding and hides the numeric percentile unless you hover or open the tray. That keeps the header under 44px while still providing access to details.

elena p: Copy harmonization: use consistent verbs across the UI. If our threshold editor uses "breach"/"warn", same words should appear in the legend and in notifications. Add a small glossary link in the legend tray to the SLO docs.

sam r: Testing asks: include checks at 80% zoom, 125% zoom, and high-contrast Windows mode. Also test with VoiceOver + NVDA.

ux-bot: design-checklist: Ensure focus outline >=3px, interactive icons have discernible text, color contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text, legend textures not removed in Windows high-contrast, tray implements aria-modal or role="dialog" and focus trap.

aria chen: Thanks team. Noah / Sam can you draft a tiny PR that: 1) replaces dots with micro-pills + SVG texture; 2) adds collapsible legend tray with focus management; 3) updates preview button tooltip & DOM order; 4) compact-mode CSS to keep header <=44px. Attach before/after screenshots and a short accessibility test matrix.

noah g: Will do. PR expected in ~3hrs. I'll tag @aria chen and @elena p and include staging link.

elena p: Please bump the design ticket with the test matrix so QA can pick it up in the next sprint.

sam r: Awesome. Also flag performance — keep SVGs inline to avoid extra network requests.

aria chen: Cool. Tag me on the PR and I'll run a quick 10-min SRE check once it's up. :thumbsup: 

ux-bot: deploy-note: design PR #501 queued for review; staging preview link will be posted when available.
